results.corrected: As of 2026-11-18, Claude Code ships these first-party features at no extra charge. Claude Code itself is not free: it needs a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise) or pay-per-token API billing. The features are: /stats, now an alias that opens the Stats tab of /usage, with an activity heatmap, a usage streak, active days and a most-active day; /insights, which analyzes up to 200 recent local sessions and writes an HTML report on how you work (~/.claude/usage-data/report.html), with the tokens counting against your plan or API usage; /recap, a one-line session summary capped at 400 characters (an automatic recap also appears when you return to an idle session); and a custom status line whose JSON input includes rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day (used_percentage and resets_at). That data is sent only to claude.ai Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers, or behind a Claude apps gateway, and only after the session's first API response. Remote Control can send push notifications to the Claude iOS/Android app when a task finishes or Claude needs a decision. It needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan (no API keys) and is opt-in under /config.

results.note: Every feature is real and documented in first-party docs. The verdict is partly, not confirmed, for four reasons. (1) "Free" is misleading. Since v2.1.118 (Apr 23, 2026) it is an alias that opens the Stats tab of /usage. (3) The status line rate-limit fields reach only Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers (or users behind a Claude apps gateway), and only after the first API response. API-key users get none, and the docs list no Team or Enterprise access. (4) Remote Control push needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan, the Claude mobile app, and opting in under /config. On Team and Enterprise, an Owner must also turn Remote Control on. The heatmap is confirmed by a changelog fix dated Aug 25, 2026. Streaks are confirmed by the Dec 10, 2025 changelog entry ("usage streak"), and I found no later note removing them. I did not see the current Stats tab UI directly: the locally installed CLI is v2.1.4, too old to check.

results.claim: CodeBurn is a free MIT usage/cost tracker for AI coding agents with about 11,859 GitHub stars as of 2026-11-18, and it detects looping tool calls and repeatedly failing commands.
results.corrected: CodeBurn (github.com/getagentseal/codeburn) is a free, local, MIT-licensed tool that tracks AI coding token usage and cost across 37 tools and agents, with 11,859 GitHub stars as of 2026-11-18. Its opt-in Guard feature uses Claude Code hooks to catch looping tool calls (the same tool with the same input, warning at 4 in a row and stopping at 8) and repeatedly failing shell commands (warning at 3 failures and stopping at 5).

evidence.quote: stargazers_count: 11859, forks_count: 913, description: 'Free, local tool to track AI coding token usage and cost across 37 tools and agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini and more), by model, project, and task. npx codeburn', license: MIT License
Stars: 11.9k ... License: MIT

Guard is opt-in and local. `codeburn guard install` adds Claude Code hooks that warn a session once it passes $5 and stop it at $15, and do the same for a tool call stuck in a loop or a failing command retried over and over.
CodeBurn is MIT licensed and all of it is in this repository ... There is no account, no paid tier and no feature held back for one.

Loops (default warn at 4, stop at 8): the same tool called with the same input that many times in a row gets a one-time warning, then the call is stopped. ... Retries (default warn at 3, stop at 5): a shell command that already failed that many times in the session gets a one-time warning, then further runs of it are stopped.
